decisions.question: Classify September customer deposits.
decisions.answer: Contract liability (customer deposits) of 90,000: New Beginnings 60,000 (event 15 Sep) + Fresh Freedom 30,000 (event 24 Sep). Cash received is an operating inflow; no revenue in the period.
evidence: E04 04 Contracts Returns and Angry Customers.pdf

aiProposal.answer: Contract liabilities (deferred revenue) 90,000: NB-SEP 60,000 (event 15 Sep) and FF-SEP 30,000 (event 24 Sep). Cash is operating inflow; no revenue until performance in September.
aiProposal.rationale: Management booked 90,000 as August sales; no goods or service delivered by 31 Aug, so the obligation to perform is a liability.

decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 (independent analysis, original evidence only): Contract liability (customer deposits/deferred revenue) of 90,000 (NB-SEP 60,000 + FF-SEP 30,000). Operating cash inflow, not August revenue. Challenge considered: Alternative: management's 'cash is cash' view (revenue on receipt), or recognising part of the revenue for planning work already done. Rejected: no goods or service were delivered by 31 Aug, delivery is 15 and 24 Sep, and there is no evidence that any performance obligation had been partly satisfied. The founder's messages show intent to mislead.
decisions.studentReasoning: Revenue is recognised on delivery. The contracts file states that no goods or service were delivered by 31 Aug, and the founder's WhatsApp ('Book both September deposits as August sales') shows deliberate override. Both agents reached the same conclusion independently.

decisions.question: Classify Packaging machine.
decisions.answer: Capitalise as PPE (plant and machinery), cost 60,000 (invoice A-910, installed 10 May). Investing cash outflow. Depreciated from 10 May within the 24,000 period charge (D074).
evidence: E06 06 Purchases Invoices and Goods Received.pdf

aiProposal.answer: PPE - plant/equipment 60,000 (invoice A-910, installed and available 10 May); depreciate from 10 May (included in 24,000 period depreciation).
aiProposal.rationale: Management expensed it as a repair; a new machine creates a long-term productive resource. Effect shown before depreciation (depreciation captured in D056/D074).

decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 (independent analysis, original evidence only): PPE (plant and machinery), cost 60,000, depreciated from 10 May. Management's 'Repair' (expense) classification is reversed. Depreciation is included within the 24,000 schedule (D074). Challenge considered: Alternative: treat it as a repair or replacement part (management). Rejected: invoice A-910 is for a whole new machine installed 10 May that creates a long-term productive resource. The effect shown is before its share of depreciation, which is in D074.
decisions.studentReasoning: A new machine installed and available for use creates a long-term productive resource, so it is capital expenditure, not a repair. Management's 'Repair' class would understate assets and profit. The effect shown is before its share of depreciation, which is included in D074.

decisions.question: Classify Photo booth.
decisions.answer: Capitalise as PPE (equipment), cost 20,000 (invoice P-404, available for use 10 May). Investing cash outflow; depreciated from 10 May. Not marketing expense.
evidence: E06 06 Purchases Invoices and Goods Received.pdf

aiProposal.answer: PPE - equipment 20,000 (invoice P-404, available 10 May); depreciate from 10 May.
aiProposal.rationale: Management expensed as marketing; the booth is a reusable asset with multi-period benefit. Effect shown before depreciation.

decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 (independent analysis, original evidence only): PPE (equipment), cost 20,000, depreciated from 10 May, not marketing expense. Challenge considered: Strongest alternative: it is a promotional or marketing item, to be expensed like other marketing spend. Considered seriously because of its name and management's class. Rejected: invoice P-404 is for a physical asset, 'available for use' 10 May, usable across many future events and periods. Promotional-activity expensing rules apply to advertising services and catalogues, not to durable equipment. Confidence is medium because its useful life and business use are not documented.
decisions.studentReasoning: It is a durable physical asset used across many future events, which meets the capitalisation test. Expensing applies to advertising services, not equipment. Confidence is medium because no useful life is documented; if it were treated as marketing, profit would be about 20,000 lower.

decisions.question: Classify Machine belt and calibration.
decisions.answer: Repairs and maintenance expense of 10,000 (invoice R-771, 3 Jul). Not PPE. Operating cash outflow.
evidence: E06 06 Purchases Invoices and Goods Received.pdf

aiProposal.answer: Repairs and maintenance expense 10,000 (R-771, 3 Jul) - restores normal output, no capacity/life improvement.
aiProposal.rationale: Management capitalised it as PPE; restoring normal operation is an expense.

decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 (independent analysis, original evidence only): Repairs and maintenance expense of 10,000 (opex). Management capitalised it as PPE; that is reversed. Challenge considered: Alternative: capitalise it as a component replacement (the belt), because it was spent on the new machine. Rejected: invoice R-771 states the work restored normal output and did not increase capacity or extend useful life. No separate component accounting is evidenced.
decisions.studentReasoning: The invoice says the work restored normal output and did not increase capacity or extend useful life, so it fails the capitalisation test. Management's PPE classification is reversed.

decisions.question: Classify Owner villa deposit.
decisions.answer: Owner distribution of 70,000, charged to equity; financing cash outflow. Not marketing, customer research, payroll bonus or an asset. Board to consider a recovery claim against the founder.
evidence: E09 09 Loans Owner Card and Legal Problems.pdf
E10 10 Email and WhatsApp Dump DO NOT FORWARD.pdf

aiProposal.answer: Owner distribution 70,000 (equity), not expense: villa is in founder personal name and no customer meeting occurred. Consider recovery claim against founder.
aiProposal.rationale: Management presented it as marketing/research then "bonus" in payroll; personal benefit without business purpose is a distribution. Profit rises vs management, equity unchanged overall (distribution instead of expense).

decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 (independent analysis, original evidence only): Owner distribution of 70,000, charged directly to equity (financing outflow). Not marketing, customer research, payroll bonus or an asset. Challenge considered: Alternatives: (a) business marketing or research expense (founder); (b) payroll bonus; (c) a receivable from the founder, i.e. an asset. (a) is rejected because the villa is in the founder's personal name and no customer meeting occurred. (b) is rejected because there was no employment approval and the finance manager called it personal. (c) was considered because the founder left and could be pursued for recovery. It is rejected because there is no loan agreement or repayment evidence, so a recoverable asset is not supportable; a possible claim is disclosed. The effect is measured against management booking it as an expense (payroll 'bonus'). Equity is unchanged, because distribution and expense both reduce equity.
decisions.studentReasoning: The villa is in the founder's personal name and no customer meeting occurred. The founder relabelled it first 'marketing' and then 'bonus' after the finance manager called it personal. A bonus needs employment approval, which is absent. No loan agreement supports a receivable from the founder.

decisions.question: Classify Owner card spending.
decisions.answer: Owner distribution of 40,000 (equity; financing outflow). Together with the villa it forms the same 110,000 labelled 'founder bonus' in the payroll file. It is counted once, not as extra payroll.

aiProposal.answer: Owner distribution 40,000 (equity) - personal card spending with no business evidence.
aiProposal.rationale: Included by management in 110,000 founder "bonus" payroll without employment approval; unsupported personal spending is a distribution.

decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 (independent analysis, original evidence only): Owner distribution of 40,000 (equity, financing outflow). It forms part of the same 110,000 'founder bonus' (villa 70,000 + card 40,000), so the bonus is not additional cash or expense. Challenge considered: Alternative 1: part of the card spend is legitimate business expense. Rejected: no receipts or business purpose were supplied, and the evidence rule treats owner spending as a distribution unless supported. Alternative 2: the 110,000 founder bonus is extra payroll cash on top of the villa and card. Rejected: the bank shows no 110,000 payment, the bank payroll line of 231,000 equals staff cash paid only, 70,000 + 40,000 = 110,000 exactly, and the WhatsApp 'Call it a bonus' refers to the villa.
decisions.studentReasoning: There are no receipts and no business purpose. The evidence rule treats personal owner spending as a distribution unless supported. The bank shows no separate 110,000 payment, and bank payroll of 231,000 equals staff cash only, so 70,000 + 40,000 = the 110,000 'bonus'.

decisions.question: Classify Physical product materials consumed.
decisions.answer: Cost of goods sold of 405,000: physical materials consumed on valid delivered sales, relieved from inventory. The 22,000 damaged-stock write-off is shown separately.
evidence: E06 06 Purchases Invoices and Goods Received.pdf

aiProposal.answer: Cost of goods sold 405,000 - physical materials consumed on valid delivered sales, relieved from inventory (opening 80,000 + purchases 459,000).
aiProposal.rationale: Management mixed materials and wages in an "approximate" 620,000 line; correct treatment is COGS from inventory on delivered sales only. Reclassification within P&L; net effect vs management not separately determinable, shown as 0.

decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 (independent analysis, original evidence only): Cost of sales (COGS) of 405,000: materials consumed on valid delivered sales. The remainder of purchases stays in inventory (closing book value 112,000 after the 22,000 write-off). Materials on undelivered September events are not expensed. Challenge considered: Alternative: derive COGS by the periodic method from the physical count (80,000 + 459,000 - 121,000 good stock - 22,000 damaged = 396,000). That would give 9,000 more profit and inventory. Rejected as the base case, because 405,000 is specifically tied to valid delivered sales and the count is valued at the unupdated system cost. It is flagged as a 9,000 uncertainty. The effect against management is not separable: management reported one unreconciled 'Materials and wages' line of 620,000.
decisions.studentReasoning: 405,000 is the warehouse figure tied to delivered sales, and purchases of 459,000 are supported by third-party invoices. A periodic calculation from the count would give 396,000; that 9,000 difference is flagged as an uncertainty (D075). The effect against management is not separable, because management used one approximate 'Materials and wages' line.

decisions.question: Classify Event staff payroll.
decisions.answer: Cost of sales (direct cost of Divorce Victory Party events) of 80,000; cash paid 75,000, accrued 5,000. Not administrative expense.

decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 (independent analysis, original evidence only): Cost of sales (direct service cost of Divorce Victory Party events) of 80,000, not administrative expense. Accrued unpaid 5,000 (80,000 - 75,000). Challenge considered: Alternative: keep it in admin (management), because staff may also do non-event work. decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 (independent analysis, original evidence only): No. Management profit of 312,000 includes 90,000 of undelivered deposits and 50,000 of loan proceeds, and omits costs. Corrected profit is 65,000. Any earn-out must use the corrected, evidence-based accounts; consider a clawback for the 110,000 of distributions.
